name: Daily Mail cryptic crossword, book 2 No 54

book.title: Daily Mail New Cryptic Crosswords, volume 2

clue.text: Almost bored working out the flow of life

indicators.note: working something out means solving or reorganising it, so the preceding letters get rearranged

blocks.note: both words taken letter for letter as the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone nearly bored to death by trying to work out the meaning of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' looks like a deletion signal telling you to trim 'bored', but it is part of the fodder: ALMOST BORED has exactly the eleven letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood carries oxygen around the body, so its circulating stream is poetically what keeps a creature alive.

clue.text: What and where to put most progressive effort

definitions.text: What and where to put most progressive effort

blocks.clueFragment: What and where to put most progressive effort
blocks.note: surface reading: advice on where to direct one's greatest effort to make progress
setter's reading: the thing you put (your finest walking limb) and the direction you put it, ahead of you

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is an idiom; the clue splits it into the 'what' (the best foot) and the 'where' (forward), with 'most progressive' hinting at both best and ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To put your best foot forward is an idiom for trying hard and making the strongest possible start or impression.

clue.text: As natural as church music?

definitions.note: a whimsical reading: like the music of the church instrument, an adjective

blocks.note: first meaning: grown without artificial chemicals, unprocessed
second meaning, flagged by the question mark: jokingly, of the big pipe instrument played in church

explanation.surface: A wondering comparison between something wholesome and the sound of a hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: the word for unprocessed produce looks as if built from the church instrument plus an adjective ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Organic produce is grown without synthetic chemicals, so the word commonly describes anything unadulterated and unforced.

clue.text: Force to approach the big house

definitions.note: a verb phrase in the clue; the answer here is the noun for the approach road

blocks.note: first meaning: to push or compel something onward
second meaning: the private road leading up to a mansion

explanation.surface: Someone being made to walk up to a grand country house.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to propel or compel; as a noun it is the private roadway leading up to a residence.

clue.text: Explain how to make a bishop

definitions.note: a phrase for the act; the answer is the verb

blocks.note: first meaning: to put into plainer or other words
second meaning: the church term for moving a bishop to a different see

explanation.surface: A request for instructions on how bishops are appointed.
explanation.walkthrough: In Church of England usage a bishop is moved from one diocese to another by this process, so the surface's 'make a bishop' is about relocating one, not creating one.
explanation.definitionFit: Rendering meaning into other words clarifies it, and the ecclesiastical sense is the formal transfer of a bishop between dioceses.

clue.text: Beg for rent adjustment so as to have food

indicators.note: an adjustment alters the arrangement, so the word before it has its letters reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
to have food is to dine

explanation.surface: A hungry tenant pleads for a rent reduction so they can afford to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat someone is to plead with them earnestly, a formal synonym for asking humbly.

clue.text: Big break in dictator's supposed weaponry

definitions.note: the answer completes the phrase weapons of ... rather than naming the weapons

blocks.note: first meaning: breaking on a huge scale, not a lucky chance
second meaning: the alleged arsenal of Saddam Hussein before the 2003 Iraq war

explanation.surface: A dictator's lucky breakthrough with weapons nobody is sure exist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big break' sounds like a stroke of luck but means large-scale breaking; the second half points to the 'weapons of ...' Saddam Hussein was claimed to have.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means devastation on a huge scale and completes the well-known expression about arms Iraq allegedly held.

clue.text: Bad actor held up by dismissed jumbo pilot

indicators.note: in a down entry, holding something up lifts it so it reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a ham is an actor who overacts badly
a batsman who is dismissed is out

explanation.surface: An incompetent performer is upstaged by a pilot of a jumbo jet who has just been sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo' looks like an aircraft, but it is an elephant, and the pilot is the person who drives one.
explanation.definitionFit: A mahout is the keeper and rider who steers an elephant, here playfully called a jumbo's pilot.

clue.text: Turn green when you start to show animation

indicators.note: to turn something is to change its order, so the colour word is rearranged
the start of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of the pronoun

explanation.surface: Advice to blush or go pale, or perhaps to go green with envy, as you begin acting.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation here means liveliness and vigour, which is what having plenty of pep and vitality amounts to.

clue.text: Fool for instance needing first-rate weapon

blocks.note: an ass is a foolish person
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
A1 means first-rate, with the digit read as the letter I

explanation.surface: An idiot, say, who needs a top-quality weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is the old Lloyd's Register top grade, so first-rate; in crosswords the 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender spear used by southern African peoples, so it is a kind of weapon.

clue.text: Head off champion worker

indicators.note: taking the head off a word cuts away its opening letter

blocks.note: a partisan champions a cause, as a committed supporter

explanation.surface: Instructions to stop or behead a champion craftsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion' reads as an adjective praising the worker, but it is the noun for a supporter who loses his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual tradesperson, so a particular kind of worker with a craft.

clue.text: The vehicle in front

blocks.note: first meaning: a covered road vehicle for goods
second meaning: the leading part of an army or movement

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase, a car ahead of you; split it after 'vehicle'.
explanation.definitionFit: A van is a delivery lorry, and the word also shortens vanguard, the leading position of an advancing force.

clue.text: The fault of the receiver

blocks.note: taken as written
a fence is criminal slang for someone who receives stolen goods

explanation.surface: Blaming whoever caught the ball or took the phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receiver' suggests a telephone or a footballer; it is the underworld dealer in stolen property.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence is a wrongdoing or breach of a rule, so a fault for which someone is to blame.

clue.text: One lays out money to become a poet

blocks.note: first meaning: a person who pays out cash
second meaning: Stephen ..., the twentieth-century English poet

explanation.surface: Someone spends their savings in an attempt to become a writer of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephen Spender was an English poet of the 1930s generation alongside Auden.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who disburses cash is literally a spender, and Spender is also the surname of a well-known English writer of verse.

clue.text: It's as well to become an all-rounder

blocks.note: taken as written
the letter O is round all the way round

explanation.surface: It is good for a cricketer to turn into someone who can both bat and bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: An all-rounder in cricket is a player good at batting and bowling; here it is read as the completely round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means also or in addition, the same sense as the phrase meaning additionally.

clue.text: She's covered by the usual customs declaration

indicators.note: what is covered by a phrase lies within it, so the letters sit inside a later word

blocks.note: surface padding that sets the scene at the border
letters three to seven of this word

explanation.surface: A woman hides behind the routine paperwork at customs.
explanation.definitionFit: Clara is a woman's given name, so a female person who can be referred to as she.

clue.text: Car providing standing when one gets caught having a gun

blocks.note: auto is short for automobile
a mat is something laid down to stand on
the Roman numeral one
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A getaway car scene in which someone is arrested while carrying a firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: The car supplies the first chunk, and the answer is also a word for a car with self-changing gears, which adds to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An automatic is a self-reloading firearm such as a pistol, firing repeatedly while the trigger is held.

clue.text: Be grateful for farm accommodation that's delicious

blocks.note: ta is informal British for thank you
a sty is the pen where pigs are housed

explanation.surface: A guest thanking a farm for a lovely stay.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta is everyday British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasty describes food with a pleasing flavour, which is exactly what delicious means.

clue.text: Not in good shape for a French seizure

blocks.note: un is the French for a
a fit is a sudden attack or convulsion

explanation.surface: Someone too out of condition to cope with a French medical emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out of condition physically, lacking health or fitness, is what the adjective describes.

clue.text: One has to decide if I'm pure rubbish

indicators.note: rubbish is used as a verb meaning to trash, so the words before it get scrambled

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone who must judge whether a claim of innocence is nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: An umpire is the official who makes rulings in a game such as cricket or tennis, a person whose role is judging.

clue.text: Act as deceiver more than once

definitions.note: a cryptic reading of the hyphenated verb, two times

blocks.note: first meaning: to be unfaithful to a partner
second meaning: read literally, on two occasions

explanation.surface: A cheat who has betrayed people repeatedly.
explanation.definitionFit: To two-time is to cheat on a lover with someone else, while split literally the phrase means twice.

clue.text: Lock a girl right inside

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so the short letter is put in the girl's name

blocks.note: Tess is a girl's name, as in Hardy's novel
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Locking a girl in her room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' sounds like a verb from the surface, shutting the girl in; it is the noun for a curl of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock of hair, so the two words are synonyms for a strand or curl.

clue.text: Consumer item as held up by custom

indicators.note: in a down entry, holding a word up lifts it so it reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: taken as written
usage is established custom or practice

explanation.surface: A shopping item stuck in customs, delayed by import rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumer item' looks like economics jargon; read it as something that is consumed, eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A sausage is a food that gets eaten, so cheekily it is an item for a consumer, one who consumes.

clue.text: Make fun of a supporter

blocks.note: first meaning: to tease someone
second meaning: a curved bone or strut that holds up a structure

explanation.surface: Teasing a football fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a fan; it is a structural support, such as one of the bones of the chest or a strut in a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To rib is to tease playfully, and a rib is a bone or beam that props up a framework.

clue.text: Take quite a time to become a member

definitions.note: split as two words, be long
the answer means be a member, usually with 'to'

blocks.note: first meaning: split in two, to stay a while or be slow
second meaning: to be part of a group

explanation.surface: Membership of a club taking ages to come through.
explanation.definitionFit: To belong to a club is to be one of its members, while split it means to take a long while.

clue.text: Act according to fashion

blocks.note: per means as specified by, as in 'per instructions'
to fashion is to shape or form

explanation.surface: Behaving as the latest style dictates.
explanation.definitionFit: To perform is to act on a stage, play a role, or carry out a deed, matching the verb.

clue.text: Relative replacing the French by the Italian in pursuit of firm governing body

indicators.note: replacing one thing by another swaps them, so one article is exchanged for the other within the relative
being in pursuit means coming behind, so the relative follows the firm

blocks.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company
an uncle is a family relative
le is French for the
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: A family member muscles in on a company board, ousting the French in favour of an Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: The French article at the end of the relative is swapped for the Italian one, and the result goes after the firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A council is an elected or appointed assembly that administers a town or organisation, so a body that governs.

clue.text: Bird at the end of the garden to hit on the head

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which is all that is taken

blocks.note: the crow is a common black bird
the final letter of garden

explanation.surface: A bird at the bottom of the garden to be swatted on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Crown is informal for striking someone on the top of the skull, the crown being that part of the head.

clue.text: One might go out to take it in some manner

definitions.text: One might go out to take it

blocks.clueFragment: One might go out to take it
blocks.note: first meaning: people step outdoors to take this, for fresh breathing
second meaning: a demeanour

explanation.surface: Someone going out to fetch something in a particular way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take the air' is an idiom for going out for a breath of fresh atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a person's bearing or demeanour, and the stuff we breathe is what we take on a stroll.

clue.text: One has no illusions about a lot of names

blocks.note: re means concerning, about
a list is a lot of names written down

explanation.surface: A cynic unimpressed by a long roll-call of celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist sees things as they are, without fantasy or wishful thinking, so is free of illusions.

clue.text: Not the month for an award given by the speaker

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the noun

indicators.note: not having something means it is left out, so the month is removed from the award

blocks.note: Dec is the calendar abbreviation for December
a decoration is a medal or honour

explanation.surface: An awards ceremony where the honour is presented by the speaker at the wrong time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal public address, which is what a speaker delivers to an audience.

clue.text: Mining business causing much worry

blocks.note: first meaning: a firm working far underground
second meaning: great anxiety

explanation.surface: A colliery company in trouble, giving everyone sleepless nights.
explanation.definitionFit: A concern is a business firm, and one digging far down is deep; the phrase usually means serious anxiety.
